newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Konka 1997 sales seen jumping 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Konka 1997 sales seen jumping 40 pct.

text.p: Konka Group Co Ltd, one of China's leading colour television makers, expects sales to rise 40 percent in 1997 to more than 7.0 billion yuan ($843 million), the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Friday.
The Shenzhen-based group aimed to produce 3.3 million colour televisions this year, compared with 2.5 million sets in 1996, the newspaper quoted Konka chairman Ren Kelei as saying.
Konka planned to focus on big-screen colour sets this year, Ren said but gave no profit forecast.
In a separate report in the Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin, company officials said Konka would continue to lower prices through cutting costs. The newspaper gave no further details.
Konka survived a cut-throat price war among television makers last year, boosting its market share to 13 percent in 1996 from nine percent the year before, earlier figures show.
Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliance Co Ltd, China's largest television producer, started the price war in March 1996 when it slashed retail prices by an average of 10 percent.
Konka matched Changhong's cuts in June 1996 and posted a net profit of 346 million yuan for that year, up from 268 million yuan the year before under international accounting standards.
